title: Open reduction towers and the strict augmented tensor square
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$ and $P\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Write $j_!^{A_n}$ for finite-coefficient extension and $J$ for its simultaneous strict-system version. There is a canonical isomorphism $r_\bullet:Q_X(j_!K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JQ_U(K)_\bullet$ of derived strict systems, whose $n$-th component is the $A_n$-linear open scalar comparison
$$r_n:(j_!K)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^{A_n}K_n.$$
Its inverse is the open-unit transpose for $B_X\to(A_n)_X$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, def-sf-open-reduction-coefficient-mate]; $r_\bullet$ is the comparison $r_j(K)$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Scalar restriction commutes with these open extensions and all quotient transitions. Both $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$. Moreover $\mathcal H^q(j_!^{A_n}K_n)=j_!^{A_n}\mathcal H^q(K_n)$; every cohomological interval for $K_n$ also works for $j_!^{A_n}K_n$, uniformly in $n$ [lem-sf-open-finite-constructibility-interval]. A finite locally closed constructible partition for a cohomology sheaf on $U$ extends to one on $X$ by adding the reduced closed complement with zero module; restriction intersects a partition with $U$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. No finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed.
Set $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P$, $H_U=K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P$ and use the inverse-open-unit-transpose isomorphism $\gamma^B:H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!H_U$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Put
$$T_\bullet=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_n((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}P_n)\bigr)_n,\quad S_\bullet=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_n(K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_U}j^*P_n)\bigr)_n.$$
Let $c_T:\Delta H\to T_\bullet$ and $c_S:\Delta H_U\to S_\bullet$ be the strict tensor quotient augmentations on these representatives [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]; $\Delta$ is the constant-tower functor. Through $r_\bullet$ and tensor change of rings [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], reduction of $\gamma^B$ is the simultaneous finite open tensor isomorphism $\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_\bullet$, and
$$\gamma_\bullet\circ c_T=J(c_S)\circ\Delta(\gamma^B).$$
This equality holds for the simultaneous augmented strict complex-system maps, hence in their derived category. Under balanced tensor identifications the coefficient-change map is $(x\otimes y)\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, preserving homogeneous degrees, signs and every quotient transition. In particular the equality includes the strict augmentation, rather than only its finite derived evaluations.

proof.text:
Choose flat-term K-flat complexes $Q\to K$ on $U$ and $F\to P$ on $X$. The open semilinear tensor-model lemma gives a flat-term K-flat representative $j_!Q$ of $j_!K$ and a chain isomorphism
$G=\operatorname{Tot}(j_!Q\otimes F)\cong j_!\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes j^*F)=j_!G_U$.
Restriction and coefficient pullback preserve flat-term K-flat representatives, so $j^*F$, $Q_n=Q\otimes B_{n,U}$ and $F_n=F\otimes B_{n,X}$ compute the indicated derived objects. Here $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$; coefficient pullback is applied on the identity topos with its map $B_W\to B_{n,W}$. The chain isomorphism is the ordinary slice tensor isomorphism, in the inverse-open-unit-transpose normalization of $\gamma^B$. All complexes remain unbounded; these are computational K-flat choices, not a finite-Tor assumption on $K$ or $P$.

proof.text: Apply the strict semilinear tensor-model statement to $Q$. It supplies a single $A_\bullet$-linear chain isomorphism $r_Q:((j_!Q)\otimes B_{n,X})_n\to J(Q_n)_n$ with formula $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$, commuting with all quotient maps and scalar units. Its evaluations localize to the canonical open scalar comparisons. Their inverses are the open-unit transposes by the open tensor normalization, hence have exactly the normalization specified by the coefficient-mate definition. Since $K$ is complete, the integral open reduction comparison identifies this localization with the already specified $r_j(K)$ and proves that $j_!K$ is complete. This constructs $r_\bullet$ as a simultaneous system map; it is not assembled from unrelated derived evaluations.

proof.text: Scalar restriction commutes with the open extensions in the statement: on each extension-presheaf summand it retains the same underlying abelian group, with $B_X$ acting through $B_X\to B_{n,X}$; this is the same action obtained by first restricting scalars on the open and then extending. The restriction maps and quotient transitions are the same maps on these summands. Sheafification has the same underlying additive sheaf with this induced action, so the identification also holds for the module sheaves and termwise for complexes and strict systems. In particular $r_Q$ retains its $A_n$-linear identification before scalar restriction, as well as its strict $B_X$-linear tower identification afterwards.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k$), so finite type over $k$ implies that $X$ is locally Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian lemma. The definition of finite type gives quasi-compactness over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence $X$ is Noetherian. The open $j$ is therefore quasi-compact. For each $n$, apply the finite open constructibility-interval lemma to $K_n$: via $r_n$ it gives constructible cohomology of $(j_!K)_n$, the equality $\mathcal H^q(j_!^{A_n}K_n)\cong j_!^{A_n}\mathcal H^q(K_n)$, the same interval as $K_n$, and exactly the asserted partition with the reduced closed complement and zero sheaf. The single interval in the integral definition therefore works for every $n$. Combining this with completeness from step 2 proves $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$. Apply the immersion completed-pullback comparison to the open immersion $j$ and $P$: it gives ordinary exact $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$ with the same uniform interval and quotient identifications. Its strata are the intersections of the original strata with $U$, omitting empty intersections.

proof.text:
The complexes $G$ and $G_U$ are K-flat: for an acyclic complex $C$, reassociation identifies $(Q_1\otimes Q_2)\otimes C$ with $Q_1\otimes(Q_2\otimes C)$, which is acyclic successively by K-flatness of $Q_2$ and $Q_1$. This applies to $(j_!Q,F)$ and $(Q,j^*F)$ from step 1. Thus their ordinary coefficient quotients compute derived reduction. For two module sheaves $M,N$ over $B$ and a coefficient algebra $A$, the balanced maps
$(M\otimes_BN)\otimes_BA\longrightarrow(M\otimes_BA)\otimes_A(N\otimes_BA)$,
$(x\otimes y)\otimes a\longmapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$,
and $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\longmapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$
are inverse: balancing moves $b$ between the two $A$ factors and moves every $B$ scalar across either tensor. This calculation is compatible with restrictions and thus gives the sheaf tensor maps. Apply it to each homogeneous summand of $G$ and $G_U$, with $A=B_{n,W}$. Neither map permutes $x$ and $y$, so both preserve bidegrees $(a,b)$ and intertwine $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes dy$. They therefore give chain isomorphisms between the quotient of the ordinary total tensor and the finite total tensor. They also commute with $B_{m,W}\to B_{n,W}$ because that map sends $ab$ to the product of the images and sends $1$ to $1$. These are the canonical derived coefficient-tensor identifications: on the K-flat representatives of step 1 they are precisely the tensor-pullback comparison.

proof.text:
At each coefficient stage the ordinary slice tensor isomorphism of the open semilinear tensor-model statement gives $\operatorname{Tot}(j_!^{A_n}Q_n\otimes_{B_{n,X}}F_n)\cong j_!^{A_n}\operatorname{Tot}(Q_n\otimes_{B_{n,U}}j^*F_n)$. Compose it with $r_Q$ on its first factor to obtain the simultaneous $\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\to JS_\bullet$. To identify it with reduction of $\gamma^B$, use the extension-presheaf summand labeled by $V\to U$. There the ordinary open tensor map sends $[x]\otimes y$ to $[x\otimes j^*y]$: its inverse restricts to $u_Q\otimes1$ and hence is the specified open-unit adjunct, not a separately chosen isomorphism. Under the balancing maps of step 5, reduction followed by this finite open tensor map sends
$([x]\otimes y)\otimes a\longmapsto[(x\otimes a|_U)\otimes(j^*y\otimes1)]$.
First applying the ordinary open tensor map and then reduction gives the same expression. The sheaf tensor and extension constructions extend these equal bilinear formulas to the sheaves. They preserve bidegrees and satisfy the same signed differential equation as in step 5. Replacing $a$ by its quotient image gives the identical formula at every lower index. Thus the maps and their inverses form chain isomorphisms of strict systems, and the equality identifying reduction of $\gamma^B$ holds for these chain-system maps.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; underived map in sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor. Agent calculation of the simultaneous tensor quotient augmentation.

proof.text: The tensor quotient augmentations on $G$ and $G_U$ are obtained by the scalar units in the reduction tower and the balancing maps of step 5. On a homogeneous extension generator, the upper augmentation sends $[x]\otimes y$ to $([x]\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. Applying $\gamma_\bullet$ sends this to $[(x\otimes1)\otimes(j^*y\otimes1)]$. The other route first sends $[x]\otimes y$ to $[x\otimes j^*y]$ under $\gamma^B$ and then to exactly $[(x\otimes1)\otimes(j^*y\otimes1)]$ under $J(c_S)$. The coefficient is $1$ at every level and every quotient map preserves $1$, so this is an equality of the simultaneous augmented strict systems. There is no degree interchange, and the signed differential was checked in steps 5 and 6. The tensor-completion normalization specifies these very scalar-unit tensor augmentations (first Roos coordinate the displayed tensor, shifted coordinate zero). Consequently $\gamma_\bullet\circ c_T=J(c_S)\circ\Delta(\gamma^B)$ before localization. Applying the localization functor preserves that equality, proving it in the derived category of strict systems as asserted; no faithfulness of separate finite evaluations and no commutation of $j_!$ with products or inverse limits is needed.
